BCRED.text: BCRED has elected to be taxed as a regulated investment company. Its payouts come mainly from interest on its loans and are generally taxed as ordinary income in the year they're paid, reported on Form 1099-DIV. The return-of-capital deferral this tool models generally doesn't apply.

source.name: BCRED Form 10-K, year ended December 31, 2025
source.page: Item 1: Material U.S. Federal Income Tax Considerations

BXPE.text: BXPE's feeder is treated as a partnership for U.S. tax purposes. Investors are taxed on their share of the fund's income, gains and losses whether or not anything is paid out, and receive a Schedule K-1 rather than a 1099.
